newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway debt restrained by strong October CPI.
newsitem.headline: Norway debt restrained by strong October CPI.

text.p: Norway's short- and medium-term debt closed moderately lower in active trade, following stronger-than-expected October consumer prices.
But the yield on the long 2007-bond shed one basis point after traders saw most of the rise in consumer prices came from higher energy costs.
Statistics Norway announced a 1.7-percent year-on-year growth in October consumer prices, stronger than the 1.5-percent average increase expected in a Reuters poll.
The Central Bank announced an average accepted yield on a three-billion-crowns auction in the 2001 bond at 5.56 percent.
"Three minutes before we were about to bid, they released stronger consumer prices than expected," said one dealer in a major Norwegian bank.
"But after scrutinizing the data, discovering that most of the rise stemmed from higher energy prices, some optimism returned. Underlying inflation is still very mild."
The krone was stable against the European Currency Unit, closing at 101.3 compared to 101.4 on Friday.
